extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers; citizens interested in foreign affairs and the French constitutional text
extracted.subtask_description: A scanned/ocr newspaper page combining foreign‑affairs reporting (Big Four/Paris conferences) and a long excerpt of the French constitutional text (declaration of rights and articles on organization of government).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality before the law (Article I)
rubrics_metrics.description: All men are born and free and equal before the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes explicit guarantee of equality; later articles extend equality guarantees to women and to all inhabitants of the French Union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereignty of the people (Article II)
rubrics_metrics.description: The source of all sovereignty rests essentially in the people; no individual or body can exercise authority not expressly derived from the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law is an expression of the national will exercised through elected representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom defined and limited (Article III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom is the faculty of doing all that does not infringe on the rights of others; freedom may be subject to conditions determined by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes individual liberty as subject to legal limits protecting others' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law guarantees equal exercise of freedoms (Article IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: The law guarantees equal exercise for all freedoms and rights enumerated and cannot infringe upon them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that statutory law must preserve the equality of rights and freedoms set out in the declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of movement and residence (Article V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person has the right to settle any place and move freely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General guarantee of internal freedom of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to asylum (Article VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person persecuted in violation of the freedoms and rights guaranteed by the declaration has the right of asylum in the territories of the Republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames asylum as a right for those persecuted for violating declared freedoms and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inviolability of the home (Article VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: The home is inviolable; no search can take place except under conditions provided by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects domicile against arbitrary searches; further procedural rules would be in law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy of correspondence (unnumbered article nearby)
rubrics_metrics.description: The secrecy of correspondence is inviolable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short declaratory protection for private correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal procedural protections / detention limits (Article IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: No one can be pursued, arrested or detained except in cases determined by law and according to prescribed forms; no one can be kept in detention without appearing within 48 hours before a judge and without monthly motivated decisions confirming detention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides prompt judicial review of detention and requires motivated periodic confirmation of continued detention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of cruel or excessive constraint (part of Article IX area)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any severity or constraint not necessary to apprehend the person, or moral/physical brutality during interrogation, is forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes limits on interrogation and detention practices; persons violating these rules will be punished and held personally responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No retroactive law; presumption of innocence; proportional penalties (Article X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Law can have no retroactive effect; every accused person is presumed innocent until declared guilty; no one can be punished twice for the same act; penalties are personal and proportionate and should aim at re‑education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic procedural criminal law protections and sentencing principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to obtain justice regardless of resources (Article XI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The law assures to all the right to obtain justice; insufficiency of resources should not be an obstacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms access to justice as a guaranteed right and not limited by means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of jurisdiction within territory (Article XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: In penal matters the identity of jurisdiction within the limits of the same territory is guaranteed to all inhabitants of the French Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guarantees jurisdictional consistency in penal cases across the territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from discrimination / freedom of conscience (Article XIII and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: No one can be disturbed because of origin, opinions, beliefs in religious, philosophical or political matters; freedom of conscience and religion is guaranteed; state neutrality and separation of church and state are affirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guarantees non‑discrimination and state neutrality in religious matters; protects freedom of belief and assembly of sects with lay control of public education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of expression (Article ? — printed nearby)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man is free to speak, write, print and publish; he may express, diffuse and defend any opinion so long as he does not abuse this right to violate others' freedoms or injure reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects press and expression subject to limits preventing abuse (defamation, injury to reputations, or violations of other guaranteed freedoms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and economic rights (preface to Section II / multiple articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every human possesses with regard to society rights that guarantee his full physical, intellectual and moral development; the law organizes the exercise of these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces a set of socio‑economic guarantees (education, health, work, family protection) later elaborated in specific articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to social protection, health and adequate living standards (Articles XXIV, XXXV region)
rubrics_metrics.description: The nation guarantees family conditions necessary for free development, protects mothers and children, guarantees hygienic measures and health care, and proclaims equality and solidarity concerning resultant charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms state obligations on social welfare, health, and family support; women are guaranteed conditions to exercise both civic and work roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to education (Article XXVII area)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization of public education at every stage is the duty of the State; education must be free and accessible to all with material aid for those who need it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education is public, free, and the state must provide material aid to ensure accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to work, just remuneration and protection of labor (Article XXIX and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man has the right to rest and leisure, to defend his interests through labor unions, to the duty to work and the right to obtain employment; working conditions must not affect health or dignity; remuneration must be just according to quality and quantity of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects labor rights, unionization, just pay, limits on adolescent labor, and workplace health/safety concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to strike (Article XXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to strike is recognized for all within the scope of laws that govern it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmative recognition subject to organizing law/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of association (Article XVII/XXXVII area)
rubrics_metrics.description: All men have the right to associate freely unless their association infringes the freedoms guaranteed by the declaration; no one can be forced to join an association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects freedom of association while forbidding associations that violate other guaranteed freedoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of ownership limited by social good (Article XXXVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership is an inviolable right to use, enjoy and dispose of property guaranteed by law, but it must not be exercised contrary to the social good or to prejudice the safety, liberty, existence or property of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows that enterprises which become effective monopolies or public service may become community property; ownership subject to social obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑discrimination in public office and access (Article XVIII region)
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to public functions is guaranteed without other condition than aptitudes; public functions are open to all citizens enjoying political rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms merit/aptitude as basis for public office and prohibits discriminatory restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political structure and legislative primacy (multiple articles: e.g., Article LXVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Assembly alone has the right to legislate; laws apply to departments and overseas territories unless otherwise stipulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets legislative monopoly of the Assembly and describes territorial application of laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law‑making and drafting procedures (Articles LXII–LXV region)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Premier and Deputies have the right to propose laws; the National Assembly studies drafts informed by commissions; the Economic Council must be consulted on drafts and national economic plan matters; procedures and timelines for consultation and debate are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies institutional roles in drafting and pre‑legislative consultation, including notice periods and consultation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules on executive accountability and confidence (Articles LXXIX–LXXXI region)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council of Ministers is collectively and individually responsible for actions; a vote of censure implies collective resignation of the Cabinet; the Assembly can pronounce dissolution by a qualified majority under stated conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines mechanisms of parliamentary control over the executive, motions of censure, and dissolution procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential powers, election, and terms (Articles LXXXIV–CIV region)
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the Republic is elected for seven years (re‑election allowed once), signs and ratifies treaties, appoints the President of the Council, represents the French Union and presides over certain councils; procedures for replacement and temporary exercise of powers are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details constitutional competences and procedural safeguards for presidential functions and succession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial responsibility and penal accountability (Articles LXXXVII and LXXXVIII area)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers are responsible under penal code for crimes and infractions committed in exercise of their functions; ministers can be accused by the National Assembly under prescribed procedures and tried before the High Court of Justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes criminal accountability for ministers and special procedures for prosecution.
